# CORTEX NEO · Conky Theme

**Your Linux desktop, in real time.**

[English](README.md) · [Español](README.es.md)

[![CI](https://github.com/JorgeTato99/cortex-neo-conky-theme/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JorgeTato99/cortex-neo-conky-theme/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[![Python 3.11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11%2B-6de4ef.svg)](pyproject.toml)

</div>

CORTEX NEO turns system information into independent neon desktop cards. Python collects shared telemetry; Lua and Conky draw historical graphs, optional hardware details and local diagnostic tools. Missing tools and sensors remain absent or unavailable rather than becoming invented readings.

## What it shows

- **System:** distribution/version, kernel/build, architecture and clock.
- **CPU:** model, cores/threads, temperature, utilization history and top processes.
- **RAM:** usage, available memory, optional module/type/speed details and grouped application RSS.
- **GPU:** detected model, driver and available sensors; utilization/VRAM or frequency with their actual units.
- **Storage:** filesystem usage and mounted/unmounted devices, distinguishing drives with the same model.
- **Network and Docker:** traffic history, separate Engine/Desktop counts and Compose groups.
- **Versions/builds:** installed applications and toolchains; empty categories disappear and long inventories paginate.
- **Weather and calendar:** seven-day forecast for a manually configured city and a monthly calendar highlighting today.

Live metrics update every **2 seconds**. Mount changes refresh storage inventory; full disk scans run every 30 seconds. Versions and weather use longer cadences to keep the hot path light.

## Quick installation

Requires **Linux with a graphical session, user systemd and Python 3.11+**. Automatic package profiles cover Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 and Debian 12/13.

Download and extract the source [ZIP](https://github.com/JorgeTato99/cortex-neo-conky-theme/archive/refs/heads/main.zip), then run from that directory:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

Run as your desktop user; only apt needs sudo. The installer prepares Conky, GTK, fonts and its own Python environment, enables user services and preserves personal settings. It does not install Docker, programming languages or GPU drivers. [Installation options and checks](docs/getting-started/installation.md).

## Make it yours

```bash
cortex-neo configure --language en --palette blue --font ubuntu
cortex-neo configure --detail-level essential
cortex-neo configure --profile compact --density comfortable
cortex-neo configure --profile full --density complete --detail-level full
```

If the command is not yet on PATH, use `~/.local/bin/cortex-neo`.

- **Ten complete palettes:** `blue`, `teal`, `green`, `yellow`, `orange`, `red`, `pink`, `purple`, `slate`, `brown`.
- **Three font profiles:** `ubuntu` (Ubuntu Sans Mono), `dejavu` (DejaVu Sans Mono), `liberation` (Liberation Mono). Missing families fall back safely; icons retain FontAwesome.
- **Independent detail level:** `essential` hides secondary specifications and builds; `full` restores them. Primary models, versions, metrics, graphs and tops remain.
- **Adaptive layout:** full/compact profiles, comfortable/complete density, landscape/portrait, opacity and card selection.

Keep the overview focused on two real desktops; explore the other colors in the separate gallery. [See all ten palettes on a real desktop](docs/reference/appearance.md).

Edit simple JSON files under `~/.config/cortex-neo/` or use the CLI. Updates preserve your choices and manually configured city. [Configuration guide](docs/getting-started/configuration.md).

## Local development and diagnostic tools

| Purpose | Command / guide |
|---|---|
| Check dependencies/session and identify installed source | `doctor` / `version` · [Guide](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md) |
| Measure dashboard CPU/RSS and payload overhead | `performance` · [Guide](docs/guides/performance.md) |
| Understand available RAM, swap, PSI and explicit PSS/USS | `memory` · [Guide](docs/guides/memory.md) |
| Inspect engines, services and Compose projects | `containers` · [Guide](docs/guides/docker-projects.md) |
| Keep a bounded before/after incident window | `incident` · [Guide](docs/guides/incidents.md) |
| Query numerical minute history | `history` · [Guide](docs/guides/history.md) |
| Measure an explicit test/build command | `run` / `tasks` · [Guide](docs/guides/tasks.md) |
| Review selected context for an agent | `context` · [Guide](docs/guides/agent-context.md) |
| Compare named environment observations | `baseline-save` / `compare` · [Guide](docs/guides/baselines.md) |
| Hide personal labels and preview a support report | `presentation` / `report` · [Guide](docs/guides/sharing.md) |

These tools are local and opt-in. Observations retain freshness and accounting limits; they do not automatically infer causes or administer processes, containers or remote machines.

## Tested machines and compatibility

| Machine | CPU / RAM | GPU | Verified system |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ryzen 7 5700X | 8 cores / 16 threads · 64 GB DDR4 | RTX 4060 Ti 8 GB | Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS · GNOME Wayland |
| Dell Latitude 5420 | Core i5-1135G7 · 16 GB DDR4 | Intel Iris Xe | Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS · GNOME Wayland |

Validation combines Python 3.11–3.15, real Lua callbacks, native ARM64 logic, four clean distribution install/render jobs and two physical Ubuntu GNOME machines. Sensor support depends on kernel, driver and permissions; AMD coverage currently uses fixtures. [Compatibility scope](docs/reference/compatibility.md) · [Tests and limits](docs/validation/testing.md).

## Privacy and manual location

Weather requires a **manually configured city**. There is no GeoIP, GPS, GeoClue or Wi-Fi location detection. Open-Meteo receives the coordinates you configure and ordinary request network information; no network-anonymity claim is made.

Personal settings, cache, screenshots and private records live outside source under XDG paths. Reports select fields for review and are never sent automatically. [Data, location and captures](docs/reference/privacy.md).

## Update and remove

Run the same installer from a newly extracted ZIP or your updated checkout, then verify the result:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
cortex-neo version
cortex-neo doctor
```

Immutable releases are prepared before switching; activation failure restores the previous runtime. `cortex-neo uninstall` removes owned installation controls while preserving personal data. [Lifecycle details](docs/getting-started/updates-and-uninstall.md).
